_scope: Base-mainnet FORK. No finality, no public visibility, no funds at risk. This demonstrates the handover mechanism. It is NOT a public-chain execution and must not be presented as one.

steps.title: Runner A is ACTIVE under customer-approved limits
Runner A executes a REAL supply through Held — budget is actually spent
steps.path: Almanak-shaped bundle -> Held admission -> runner A EIP-712 -> HeldController -> Zodiac Roles -> Safe -> Morpho

steps.title: A REAL operation is dispatched; the server receives it and drops the connection
steps.grade: REAL OPERATION + DURABLE JOURNAL + REAL LOCAL TRANSPORT AMBIGUITY (local server, NOT KeeperHub, NOT hosted)
steps.why: the request really left over a socket and the server really received it, then closed without answering. Held claimed the operation durably BEFORE any I/O, so the attempt is recoverable — but whether the work started is genuinely unknown, and an unknown is not a verified negative

steps.title: Owner FENCES the controller on chain (Held prepared it; the owner sent it)
steps.note: an adapter that merely stops dispatching is NOT a fence — the controller would still honour a signed envelope

steps.title: Handover REFUSED while the outcome is unresolved
steps.why: the machine derived this set from the durable journal, not from a list someone handed it. Activating now would either lose consumption that really happened or charge the customer twice for work that did not

steps.title: Reconciled from the controller's own consumed[] record
steps.note: the verdict comes from consumed[operationId] at a stated block, not from the transport's silence

steps.title: Bounded authority inventory, collected LIVE at the fence
Runner B pinned against the consumption actually on chain
Held PREPARES the activation and describes it; it does not sign it
steps.summary: Activate epoch 2 with runner 0x976EA74026E726554dB657fA54763abd0C3a0aa9. Remaining capacity after this change: supply 49988000000, normal withdraw 50000000000, restoration 10000000000, counts 9/5.

steps.title: Runner B is ACTIVE — Held's verified consumption survived the handover
Runner A ATTEMPTS its old authorization — the controller refuses it
steps.why: behavioural, not inferred: runner A really signed a fresh operation under its retired epoch and really sent it. The controller authorizes against the CURRENT epoch and runner, so it reverts.

steps.title: Runner B receives what it needs to continue — and no key material

resolutions.reason: consumed[operationId] is zero at the stated block

reconciliation._derivation: The operation set is derived from the durable journal for the retiring epoch. The machine re-derives it on acceptance, so a report that omits a known operation is refused.

bounded authority inventory complete and scoped to this installation
